paper.title: REFLECT: Summarizing Robot Experiences for Failure Explanation and Correction
paper.central_claim: REFLECT summarizes multisensory robot experience hierarchically and queries an LLM progressively to explain and localize failures, and the explanation guides a language planner to correct the failure (RoboFail: 100 sim + 30 real failures).

evidence.quote: we introduce REFLECT, a framework which queries LLM for failure reasoning based on a hierarchical summary of robot past experiences generated from multisensory observations
evidence.support_explanation: Author central claim (framework).

evidence.quote: We demonstrate that the LLM-based framework is able to generate informative failure explanations that assist successful correction planning.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim of explanation + correction.

evidence.quote: However, they all assume ground truth environment feedback associated with one or few actions.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: prior LLM self-reflection works need ground-truth feedback.

evidence.quote: prior works are limited as each only address a specific set of failure scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: prior failure explanation covers narrow failure sets.

evidence.quote: Extending upon prior works, our approach generates captions that are task-centric and action-centric for temporal robot sensory data in a zero-shot manner
evidence.support_explanation: Lineage: zero-shot video captioning (Socratic Models-style) extended to robot sensory data.

evidence.quote: a frame is selected if it satisfies any of the conditions below
evidence.support_explanation: Key-frame selection rule of the event-based summary (scene-graph change, audio event boundary, subgoal end).

evidence.quote: If a subgoal is not achieved, then we retrieve history observations stored in event-based summary for failure explanation as follows
evidence.support_explanation: Progressive explanation: subgoal verification then retrieval of event-level history.

evidence.quote: In case all subgoals are achieved but the task still failed, then it
evidence.support_explanation: Planning-failure branch when all subgoals pass.

evidence.quote: We assume the framework has access to ground truth object detection and state detection in simulation.
evidence.support_explanation: Privileged ground-truth perception in simulation.

evidence.quote: The real-world failure data is collected by a human teleoperating a UR5e robot arm to mimic robot policies according to a provided high-level plan.
evidence.support_explanation: Real data are teleoperated recordings, not policy rollouts; no real correction execution.

evidence.support_explanation: Co-plan metric definition (success by goal-state comparison).

evidence.quote: we ask 2 groups of users, 3 in each group to compare the ground truth failure explanation labelled in the dataset and REFLECT-generated failure explanation for each failure scenario

evidence.quote: it is less effective for handling low-level control failures

signatures.object: post-execution multisensory robot log (RGB-D, audio, robot state) -> three-level text summary (sensory-input scene graph + audio label, event-based key-frame captions, subgoal-end observations)
signatures.information: Full post-hoc log, original robot plan and goal state; sim uses ground-truth detection/state; real uses MDETR/CLIP/AudioCLIP; environment assumed static
signatures.operation: serialize detections, heuristic spatial relations and audio labels into text; select key frames on scene-graph/audio/subgoal change
signatures.conditions: task-relevant objects only; 8 hand-coded spatial relations; fixed state-label lists
signatures.selection_rule_data: key-frame rule: scene-graph change, audio event start/end, subgoal end
signatures.persistence: none (per-episode, not carried to later tasks)
signatures.claimed_effect: more informative explanations than BLIP2 captions / LLM-written summary / no-audio
signatures.failure_boundary: complex scenes beyond heuristics, low-level control failures, dynamic environments, perception errors

signatures.object: progressive failure explanation prompt chain over the summary
signatures.information: subgoal-level text first, event-level history only after a failed subgoal; goal state and original plan for planning-failure branch
signatures.operation: LLM answers Yes/No per subgoal; on No retrieve event summary and ask for explanation; if all Yes ask what is wrong with the plan
signatures.output: failure explanation and failure time step
signatures.conditions: assumes execution vs planning failure dichotomy; in planning mode assumes all actions executed
signatures.feedback: LLM verdicts over text summary (no ground-truth verifier of the Yes/No verdicts reported)
signatures.claimed_effect: higher Exp and Loc than w/o progressive and subgoal-only
signatures.failure_boundary: localization harder for planning failures that are not tied to a single step

signatures.object: explanation-conditioned correction planner (GPT-4) mapped to executable actions by sentence-embedding nearest action
signatures.information: original plan, failure explanation, final state, goal state
signatures.operation: generate correction plan from final state and run it in AI2THOR
signatures.output: correction plan executed; success by goal-state comparison
signatures.failure_boundary: correction not executed on real robot

gap.author_gap: Robots need to explain and correct failures from multimodal logs; prior failure-explanation work handles only specific failure sets and LLM self-reflection works assume ground-truth feedback for one or few actions.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and sourced from the paper's own related-work text: converting raw multisensory logs into language the LLM can reason over is the bottleneck. Nearest neighbours were not independently fetched (offline), so lineage is as cited by the authors.

gap.residue: Low-level control failures, complex scenes beyond hand-coded relations, dynamic environments, ground-truth perception in simulation, no real-robot correction.
gap.stakes: Failure explanation for debugging and autonomous correction; correction planning succeeds 42-56% without explanation vs about 80% with it in simulation.
gap.method_response: Hierarchical summary + progressive querying + explanation-conditioned correction planning.
gap.remaining_gap: Real-robot closed-loop correction; non-oracle perception in sim; comparison with published failure-explanation methods; low-level control failures.
unresolved: No head-to-head run against any published failure-explanation system; only in-house ablations.
Closest-neighbour versions not pinned locally; no independent novelty search.

matches.reason: Operation is serialization of heterogeneous sensor streams into text for a single LLM, which is C18's 'serialize a structured signal into the surface form of a mature modality'. Not a learned tokenizer/projection and no training, so the fit is partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Primary chosen by operation (multisensory-to-text interface feeding one LLM), not by the word 'unified'. decompose_and_delegate was read and rejected: the LLM is the only reasoner and no sound solver or typed verification closure exists.

executes_pattern.reason: Interface and uniform-model steps executed; learned/validated semantic units and specialist parity not shown.

resolves_problem.reason: Ablations show the summary carries needed information in 100 simulated + 30 real recordings, but sim uses ground-truth perception and no published explainer is beaten.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: C18 serialization of a foreign modality into a mature modality's surface form corresponds to K109 sensor-to-text conversion for the planner/verifier.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K109 assumes a separate frozen VLM and online planning; REFLECT uses detectors/CLIP/AudioCLIP + heuristics, adds audio, and is post-hoc.

claims.text: Hierarchical summary + progressive querying yields correct, informative failure explanations (Exp).
claims.setting: AI2THOR 100 injected failures (ground-truth perception); real 30 teleoperated recordings; GPT-4
claims.baseline_control: BLIP2 caption, w/o sound, w/o progressive, subgoal-only, LLM summary
claims.selection_vs_test: no training; dev overlap not disclosed
claims.result_denominator: Sim Exp 88.4/84.2 (exec/plan) vs best baseline 76.7/71.9; real Exp 68.8/78.6 where planning ties w/o sound at 78.6; denominators not stated (about 43/57 sim, 16/14 real inferable)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Explanation gains are visible for execution failures in sim; real planning-failure Exp shows no gain over w/o sound/subgoal-only.

claims.result_denominator: Sim Loc 96.0/80.7; real 93.8/78.6 (planning ties three baselines at 78.6)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Strong for execution failures; planning-failure localization not better than simple baselines on real recordings.

claims.text: Failure explanation guides correction planning to success.
claims.setting: AI2THOR only, correction executed from final state; goal-state success
claims.baseline_control: w/o explanation (41.9/56.1), other ablations up to 65.1/75.4
claims.allowed_conclusion: In simulation with ground-truth perception, explanation raises correction success by about 25-37 points over no explanation; vs subgoal-only the planning-failure margin is 5.3 points; no real-robot correction.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Co-plan is closed-loop in AI2THOR judged by goal-state check (ground-truth perception, privileged); explanation/localization are human-judged offline; real part has no correction execution so no transfer.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 100 author-injected AI2THOR failures with ground-truth perception, the GPT-4 hierarchical-summary pipeline gives higher human-judged explanation, localization and goal-checked correction success than in-house ablations; on 30 teleoperated real recordings it explains and localizes better than BLIP2/LLM-summary baselines but ties simple baselines on planning failures.
unresolved: author claim 'wide range of failure scenarios without assumptions on task configuration' exceeds evidence (author-designed 10+11 tasks, static scenes)
no comparison to published failure-explanation methods
assessment.reproduction_note: All numbers are author-reported; nothing reproduced by us.

G.reason: Concrete sourced bottleneck (narrow prior failure explainers; LLM reflection needing ground-truth feedback) with explicit residual limits; nearest neighbours not run head-to-head and not pinned locally, so not 4.

M.reason: Mechanism reconstructable from prompts/heuristics (hierarchy, progressive check, explanation-conditioned planner) and ablations discriminate it from naive alternatives; weak assumptions: execution-vs-planning dichotomy, Yes/No verifier reliability untested, planning mode assumes actions executed.

X.reason: Operation chain, prompts (Appendix A.3), heuristics (A.1-A.2) and information permissions (ground-truth perception in sim) are stated; failure boundary explicit. Gaps: key-frame/Yes-No verifier quality unreported, correction execution protocol brief.

measurement.reason: Closed-loop Co-plan uses goal-state truth but only in simulation with ground-truth perception; Exp depends on 6 human raters with majority vote and no agreement stats; denominators stated only as percentages; single trial per scenario; real part has no closed-loop execution.

causality.reason: Same GPT-4 and data across six one-at-a-time ablations (summary type, hierarchy level, progressive, explanation); w/o explanation is a fair control. Confounds: sound ablated only in real recordings; backbone effect not crossed with components; real planning rows tie.

holdout.reason: Training-free, but dataset and method share authors and dev overlap with the 100 scenarios/prompts is undisclosed; real recordings are a different setup but only for explanation/localization; no held-out embodiment closed loop.

statistics.reason: No variance, repeats or CI; denominators not stated; failure split only by execution/planning; rater agreement absent.

cost.reason: No LLM calls, tokens, latency or compute reported for any method; GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 shows capability not cost.

status_reason: Complete main text and appendices read; all eight items resolved.
